inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 Net Profit used as distributable earnings proxy. Flow Traders has no traditional FCF — trading capital IS the productive asset.
inputs.debt_note: $200m private credit facility drawn at SOFR+5% secured October 2025 (~EUR 186m). Cash and equivalents EUR 8.1m per FY2025 balance sheet.

historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: 3-year equity CAGR (FY2022-FY2025, +12.7%) is the primary anchor. The 5-year NTI and EPS CAGRs are negative because FY2020 was an anomalous COVID-volatility year (NTI EUR 933m vs EUR 300-486m in normal years). Equity CAGR is the most reliable metric as it reflects book value compounding through retained earnings during the Trading Capital Expansion era. The pre-COVID 6-year NTI CAGR (FY2019-FY2025) of 14.4% confirms mid-teens structural growth is achievable in the bull case.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year NTI and EPS CAGRs are negative due to the anomalous FY2020 COVID volatility base (NTI EUR 933m). The equity 5yr CAGR of 8.0% diverges from NTI/EPS 5yr by more than 30pp, but this is entirely COVID-base distortion, not a structural divergence. Divergence flagged for transparency; not a valuation concern.
historical_growth.cyclicality_note: Flow Traders earnings are highly cyclical: FY2020 NTI EUR 933m, FY2021 EUR 384m, FY2022 EUR 460m, FY2023 (low vol) EUR 300m, FY2024 EUR 468m, FY2025 EUR 486m. All scenarios anchored to mid-cycle earnings, not peak or trough.

base.description: Moderate market conditions with normal volatility. Capital expansion delivers incremental NTI. Fixed costs rise per FY2026 guidance (EUR 220-230m). Asia and digital assets grow steadily. Net profit at mid-cycle levels, decelerating toward maturity.
base.wacc_rationale: 11% reflects: risk-free rate ~3.5% (German 10yr Bund), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~1.3 for cyclical earnings, small-cap Euronext premium 0.5%. Higher than typical US comps to reflect earnings volatility and vol-dependency.

bull.description: Elevated market volatility (VIX 20+), strong capital deployment benefits, Asia expansion materially exceeds expectations, digital assets and tokenization accelerate. Structural ETP growth at high end of projections. FY2025 normalized EUR 140m base reflects expanded trading capital benefits already flowing.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10% in bull case as structural tailwinds reduce cyclical risk perception and demonstrate sustainable earnings power.

bear.description: Prolonged low-volatility environment (VIX 12-14) similar to FY2023 trough. Competitive pressure from Citadel and Jane Street intensifies in European core. Americas market remains impenetrable. Interest burden on USD credit facility weighs on net profit. Stressed EUR 100m base reflects below-mid-cycle conditions.
bear.wacc_rationale: 13% in bear case reflects materialized cyclical risk, higher leverage concern, and investor flight from volatile earnings businesses.

base.note: At EUR 27.18, the stock sits approximately at the 15% CAGR entry price in the base case (EUR 28.81). This implies fair-to-slightly-undervalued pricing on mid-cycle base assumptions.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC 9% to 13%, Columns = Terminal Growth 2.0% to 4.0%. Base inputs: FY2025 Net Profit EUR 133.6m, growth rates 10/9/8/7/6%.

probability_weighted.rationale: Base 50%: most likely outcome reflecting continued mid-cycle market conditions and incremental capital deployment benefits. Bull 25%: elevated volatility regime with Asia and digital assets exceeding expectations. Bear 25%: prolonged low-vol period materializes, competitive pressure intensifies.

valuation_context.commentary: At EUR 27.18, Flow Traders trades at 8.9x FY2025 earnings and 1.36x book value — a significant discount to US market-making peers (Virtu Financial trades at approximately 12-14x earnings). The sensitivity matrix indicates the base case intrinsic value range is EUR 32-72 across all reasonable WACC and terminal growth assumptions. The stock is sitting near the 15% CAGR entry price threshold in the base case (EUR 28.81), implying fair-to-slightly-undervalued pricing on mid-cycle normalized earnings. The primary discount appears to reflect: (1) extreme earnings cyclicality and unpredictability tied to VIX, (2) dividend suspension since July 2024 with no resumption timeline, (3) increased financial leverage via the $200m credit facility, and (4) uncertainty around Capital Markets Day strategy disclosure. Resolution of these overhangs — particularly dividend resumption and demonstration of trading capital ROI — could drive meaningful re-rating.
